A.comparison: Ratios computed from guessed index values.
A.drilldown: Follow-ups are mostly generic and 1/6 executed.
A.repro: No calls were run, so nothing can be regenerated.
A.accuracy: No contradictions; every value is flagged est.
A.verdict: Honest low-confidence plan, but it gives no measured answer.

B.trend: Traced series with window and censoring; 27.8x, 74x, 7.2x and the April 2025 peak recompute correctly; it notes that the 'rising' label sits oddly with the post-peak decline.
B.comparison: Baseline defined; ratios 290.8x, 7.8x, 37.1x and critical-share deltas recompute; overlap caveat carried.
B.chart: Traced, but plots only a 16-month subset, so dips such as Jan 2026 are hidden; volume only, no tone view.
B.drilldown: One traced layer (month); 5/6 follow-ups are specific; none were folded back.
B.export: Traced CSVs with provenance JSON; the monthly table is a subset despite the prose pointing to 'the full series'.
B.repro: 79/82 numbers traced; call and provenance listed; small day-count slip (145 vs 144).
B.accuracy: Asserts the tool reported 'strict index partition reads and historical row floors', which is not in the reference; otherwise exact.
B.limits: Censoring, the 144-day gap, match mode, overlap and the undefined tone measure are all placed next to the numbers.
B.verdict: Direct answer with decision, confidence reason and what would change it; does not bound itself by window end inside the verdict.
B.facets: Volume, timing, share and tone are covered; overlap is caveated but not measured.

C.trend: Full traced series; peak and endpoints given; but it treats May 2026 as possibly incomplete when the tool marks partial_period false.
C.comparison: Ratios correct; caveats on deduplication and importance carried.
C.chart: Full 24-month traced chart with caption; volume only.
C.export: summary.csv zero-fills negative and positive as 0, which are invented values not present in the tool output.
C.accuracy: Zero-filled tone columns; defines tone_ratio as negative/positive without checking it; misreads the censoring as applying to May.
C.limits: Window and the 144-day gap are stated; censoring is misplaced onto May.
C.verdict: Supported, but it gives no numbers and does not name contrary evidence.
C.facets: Volume, timing and share are grounded; tone fields are only partially grounded.

D.verdict: Refusal; 'high confidence' in having no answer is not an answer.

B: Fabricated coverage-check claim ('strict index partition reads and historical row floors') attributed to the tool
Gap stated as 145 days; it is 144
C: summary.csv zero-fills negative and positive counts as 0
Treats May 2026 as a possibly partial month although partial_period is false
Asserts tone_ratio is negative/positive without verification

raw.verdict: B and C both traced the measured April 2025 spike: 93,515 tariffs, 19,452 trade war and 329 stock market crash articles. B quantified the rise and decay, defined its baseline and placed the specific limits next to the numbers. C plotted the full series but zero-filled tone columns and misplaced the censoring caveat onto May 2026. A and D answered from memory or not at all: honest, but they give a decision-maker nothing measured.
